eventMetadata.context_description: Latest Israel Meteorological Service guidance and global model ensembles from ECMWF and GFS show Tel Aviv's May 4 high temperature clustering around 20-22°C, driving the even 35.5% implied probabilities across 19-23°C outcomes as traders price in short-range uncertainty. Stronger breezes or thicker clouds could limit peaks to 19°C, while quicker clearing favors 23°C; below 19°C or above requires outlier developments like unexpected showers or heat advection. New model runs and IMS updates expected twice daily will refine this tight 3-4°C spread before resolution.

AEMET guidance aligns with this range under partly cloudy conditions and light winds. Watch daily ECMWF updates and AEMET revisions for shifts in the 48-hour outlook, as spring diurnal heating adds uncertainty.
